prompt: What inspections are required during construction in Toronto?
answer:
The required inspections in Toronto depend on whether your project is classified as a small building (Part 9 of the Ontario Building Code) or a large building (Part 3 of the Ontario Building Code). 

For large buildings, the required inspections include:

**Building Inspections:**
- Footings (at completion of formwork, before pouring concrete)
- Foundations (at completion)
- Structural framing (at completion of structural framing for each storey)
- Fire separations and closures (at completion of framing for wall, floor and shaft fire separations)
- Insulation and vapour/air barrier (at completion and before installation of interior services)
- Fireplaces, gas appliances, and chimneys (at commencement of installation)
- Life safety systems (at completion of rough-in - referral to Toronto Fire Prevention)
- Occupancy (consult your inspector)
- Final interior inspection (at completion of interior construction)
- Final exterior inspection (at completion of grading, exterior finishes, etc.)

**Plumbing Inspections:**
- Site Meeting (at start of construction for special systems)
- Outside storm & sanitary sewers (at completion, before back filling)
- Water service (at completion, before back filling)
- Inside storm & sanitary sewers (at completion, ready for testing)
- Rough-in, water supply, drains, waste & vents (at completion and ready for testing)
- Occupancy (at completion of installation of all required fixtures)
- Final inspection (at completion of installation of remaining fixtures)
- Final exterior inspection (at completion of grading, exterior finishes, etc.)

[Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/when-to-call-for-inspection-of-large-buildings/]

[Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/closing-building-permits/]

You will be required to schedule a final inspection upon completion of the project to close the permit. Inspections may be requested online using the Toronto Building Inspection Requests web app. [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]

prompt: What inspections are required during construction in Toronto?
answer:
During construction in Toronto, various mandatory inspections are required to ensure compliance with the Building Code Act and the issued building and demolition permits. The specific inspections required depend on the nature of the project.

For small buildings (Part 9 of the Ontario Building Code including houses and small commercial structures), the inspections required include:

1. Footing formwork and reinforcement before pouring concrete
2. Foundation weeping tile and damp-proofing before backfilling
3. Foundation wall before backfilling
4. Drain, waste, and vent rough-in before insulation
5. Water service and backflow preventer before insulation
6. Sewer service lateral before insulation
7. Structural framing before insulation
8. Insulation and vapour/air barrier before interior finishes
9. Fire separation and continuity before interior finishes
10. Firestopping and draftstopping before interior finishes
11. Plumbing fixture installation before use
12. Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) before use
13. Electrical rough-in before insulation
14. Electrical final before use
15. Final inspection before occupancy

For large buildings (Part 3 of the Ontario Building Code), the inspections required include:

1. Footings at completion of formwork, before pouring concrete
2. Foundations at completion
3. Structural framing at completion of structural framing for each storey
4. Fire separations and closures at completion of framing for wall, floor ad shaft fire separations including closures, continuity and fire stopping and before applying the interior finishes, spray fireproofing and lay-in tiles to ceilings
5. Insulation and vapour/air barrier at completion of insulation & vapour/air barrier and before installation of interior services
6. Fireplaces, gas appliances, and chimneys at commencement of installation
7. Life safety systems at completion of rough-in of the safety systems - referral to Toronto Fire Prevention
8. Occupancy (consult your inspector)
9. Final interior inspection at completion of interior construction, life safety systems and all fire separations and enclosures
10. Final exterior inspection at completion of grading, exterior finishes, fire routes, parking, hydrants and site amenities

The cost for these inspections is included in your building permit fee. Additional inspections can be arranged through your local inspection office, but an additional fee may apply. [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/]

prompt: What is the process for applying for a building permit in Toronto?
answer:
The City of Toronto follows a five‑step workflow for a building‑permit application:

1. **Confirm that the project complies with zoning and other applicable laws** – you first check the Zoning By‑law (and any other statutes such as the Planning Act, Conservation Authorities Act, etc.) to make sure the work is allowed on the property.  
   *[Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/plan-review-process/]*  

2. **Prepare the design documents** – either draft the plans yourself (if you have the required drafting skills) or hire a qualified designer/engineer to produce the drawings, zoning declaration, tree declaration and any other required forms. All drawings must be high‑quality PDFs (no sketches).  
   *[Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]*  

3. **Submit the building‑permit application** – send the complete package (application form, plans, declarations, fees) online through the Toronto Building Intake Portal or by email to bldapplications@toronto.ca. Within one business day staff will issue a **Submission Status Letter** indicating whether the application is **sufficient** (ready for review) or **insufficient** (more information required).  
   *[Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]*  

4. **Plan review** – once the application is deemed sufficient, a Plan Examiner conducts a series of reviews:  

   - **Zoning review** – checks land‑use, building size, setbacks, parking, height, etc.  
   - **Building Code review** – verifies health & safety, fire protection, structural sufficiency, materials, plumbing and mechanical systems.  
   - **Mechanical plans examination** (if applicable) – HVAC, plumbing, drainage, sewage.  
   - **Fire‑prevention examination** (for certain multi‑family, commercial, industrial or institutional projects).  

   If the plans meet all requirements, the permit is approved; if not, a notice explains the deficiencies.  
   *[Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/plan-review-process/]*  

5. **Permit issuance and construction** – after the review is complete and all fees are paid, the permit is issued electronically. You may then begin work, schedule required inspections through the Toronto Building Inspection Requests web app, and, when the project is finished, request a **final inspection** to close the permit.  
   *[Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]*

prompt: What inspections are required during construction in Toronto?
answer:
In Toronto every construction project must go through a series of **mandatory building‑code inspections** that are triggered at specific “critical stages” of the work.  The owner or contractor is responsible for notifying the City’s Toronto Building office when the work is ready for each inspection, and the cost of these inspections is already included in the building‑permit fee【Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/】.  

Below is a summary of the inspections that are typically required during construction.  The exact list depends on the size and type of the project (Part 9 – small buildings, or Part 3 – large buildings), but the City provides a detailed schedule for large‑building projects that covers the most common elements.

---

### 1. Structural & Envelope Inspections  

| Inspection | When to Call (large‑building guide) |
|------------|--------------------------------------|
| **Footings** | After formwork is complete and **before** concrete is poured |
| **Foundations** | When foundation work is finished |
| **Structural framing** | At completion of the framing for each storey |
| **Fire separations & closures** | After framing of walls, floors and shafts, before interior finishes, spray fire‑proofing or ceiling tiles are installed |
| **Insulation & vapour/air barrier** | After insulation & vapour barrier are in place, before interior services are installed |
| **Fireplaces, gas appliances & chimneys** | At the start of their installation |
| **Life‑safety systems (e.g., fire alarm, sprinkler)** | When the rough‑in of those systems is complete (refer to Toronto Fire Prevention) |
| **Final interior inspection** | When interior construction, life‑safety systems and all fire separations/enclosures are finished |
| **Final exterior inspection** | After grading, exterior finishes, fire routes, parking, hydrants and site amenities are completed |
| **Occupancy** | Consult the inspector (usually after the above inspections are passed) |  

*All of these are listed in the City’s “When to Call for Inspection of Large Buildings” guide*【Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/when-to-call-for-inspection-of-large-buildings/】.

---

### 2. Plumbing & Drainage Inspections  

| Inspection | When to Call (large‑building guide) |
|------------|--------------------------------------|
| **Site meeting** | At the start of construction (especially for special systems such as pools, window‑washing equipment, etc.) |
| **Outside storm & sanitary sewers** | After the work is complete, **before** back‑filling and ready for testing |
| **Water service** | After the work is complete, **before** back‑filling and ready for testing |
| **Inside storm & sanitary sewers** | When the work is complete (may be partial) and ready for testing |
| **Rough‑in, water supply, drains, waste & vents** | When the rough‑in is complete and ready for testing |
| **Occupancy (plumbing)** | After all required fixtures are installed |
| **Final plumbing inspection** | After the remaining fixtures are installed |
| **Final exterior plumbing inspection** | After grading, exterior finishes, fire routes, parking, hydrants and site amenities are finished |  

*These plumbing milestones are also taken from the large‑building inspection schedule*【Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/when-to-call-for-inspection-of-large-buildings/】.

---

### 3. General Requirements for All Inspections  

* **Notice to the Chief Building Official** – Builders must give notice when the work is ready for each mandatory inspection (Ontario Building Code Subsection 1.3.5.1)【Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/】.  
* **Inspector access** – The inspector must be able to see the entire element under review; any covered work must be uncovered before the inspection can be passed【Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/】.  
* **Documentation on site** – A full‑scale coloured print of the stamped permit drawings (and any other permit‑related records) must be available for the inspector【Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/】.  
* **Scheduling** – Inspections are requested through the “Request an Inspection” portal or by phone; a minimum of 48 hours notice is required and inspections are performed Monday‑Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. (excluding statutory holidays)【Source: https://www.toronto.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/9273-Building-Permit-Guide-WEB.pdf】.  
* **Final inspection & permit closure** – A final inspection is required before the permit can be closed; an open permit can delay real‑estate transactions and may lead to enforcement actions【Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/】.

---

### 4. Small‑Building (Part 9) Projects  

The City also provides a separate “When to Call for Inspections for Small Buildings” guide for houses and small commercial structures (Part 9 of the Ontario Building Code).  The same principle applies: you must request inspections at each critical stage (e.g., footings, foundation, framing, fire‑separation, insulation, final interior/exterior, etc.), but the exact timing list is shorter and tailored to residential‑scale work【Source: About Building Inspections page mentions the small‑building guide, though the detailed list is not included in the provided evidence】.

---

**In short:**  
During construction in Toronto you must schedule a series of mandatory inspections that cover the structural frame, foundations, fire‑separation, insulation, mechanical/​plumbing systems, life‑safety systems, and final interior/exterior conditions.  Each inspection is triggered when the relevant work is complete and ready for review, and the inspector must be able to see the element and have the permit drawings on site.  Failure to obtain these inspections can cause delays, stop work orders, or enforcement actions.

prompt: Do I need a permit to build a fence in Toronto?

- **Standard fence on your own property:** No building permit required, but check Zoning By‑law for height, setbacks, etc.

- **Work in the public right‑of‑way or street storage:** May require a Landscaping Permit or Street Occupation Permit.

# Building Permit Application Process in Toronto

## The Five General Steps

1. **Determine compliance** – Check if your project complies with zoning and applicable laws [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/9273-Building-Permit-Guide-WEB.pdf]

2. **Prepare your application and drawings** – You can draft your own plans if you have the required drafting skills and knowledge of the Ontario Building Code, or hire a qualified designer [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]

4. **City review** – City staff will review your submission within one business day to determine if it's sufficient. You'll receive a Submission Status Letter by email:
   - If **sufficient**: You'll be asked to pay initial fees (by credit card over the phone), and a Plan Examiner will be assigned
   - If **insufficient**: You'll need to submit additional items before a review can start [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]

   - Zoning compliance

   - Mechanical plans (if applicable)
   - Fire prevention (for certain multi-family, commercial, industrial, or institutional projects) [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/plan-review-process/]

6. **Permit issuance** – Once your application complies with all regulations and all fees are paid, your permit will be issued electronically [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]

7. **Construction and inspections** – After receiving your permit, you may begin work. You must schedule inspections during construction and a **final inspection upon completion to close the permit** [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]

## Tips for a Smooth Application

- Apply as early as possible

prompt: What happens if I build without a permit in Toronto?
answer:
If you start construction work without a required building permit in Toronto, you could face serious and potentially costly consequences, including:

**1. "Work Without Permit" Administrative Fee**
This is an additional fee equal to 50 percent of the permit fees for the project. The fee has a minimum and maximum value that is updated periodically. [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/working-without-a-permit/]

[Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/working-without-a-permit/]

**3. Possible Undoing of Work**
You may have to undo the work that was already done. [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/working-without-a-permit/]

**4. Additional Unplanned Work**
You may have to do more work than you originally planned and budgeted for, such as additional structural or mechanical work. [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/working-without-a-permit/]

**5. Legal and Financial Issues**
You could face possible legal and/or financial issues down the road, such as impacts on selling your property or making an insurance claim. [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/working-without-a-permit/]

**Important Note:** As the homeowner, you are responsible for paying these fees or penalties yourself even if you have hired a contractor who assured you that permits were not needed. prompt: How much does a residential building permit cost in Toronto?
answer:
The cost of a residential building permit in Toronto varies depending on the **type of work** and **floor area**. Here are the specific calculation methods and rates found in the evidence:

**Fee Calculation Methods:**

*   **New houses:** Fees are based on the **total floor area** in dollars per square metre. This includes any proposed decks, fireplaces, or porches. [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/9273-Building-Permit-Guide-WEB.pdf]
*   **Additions to existing houses:** Fees are based on the **floor area of the proposed work** in dollars per square metre. [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/9273-Building-Permit-Guide-WEB.pdf]
*   **New decks, fireplaces, or detached garages:** A **flat fee** is charged regardless of size (specific amount not provided in evidence). [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/9273-Building-Permit-Guide-WEB.pdf]
*   **Finished basements:** Fees are based on the **floor area of the proposed work** in dollars per square metre. [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/9273-Building-Permit-Guide-WEB.pdf]
*   **Alterations/renovations (residential occupancies):** **$13.41 per square metre** of proposed work. [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-permit-application-guides/guides-for-other-buildings/interior-alterations-non-residential/]

**General Fee Structure:**

*   **Standard formula:** Permit fee = **SI × A**, where:
    *   SI = Service Index for the classification of proposed work (varies by occupancy type)

*   For the complete list of Service Index rates by occupancy and type, you must consult the **Toronto Building Fee index**. prompt: What is the process for applying for a building permit in Toronto?
answer:
The process for applying for a building permit in Toronto generally involves the following steps:

**1. Pre-Application Preparation**
- Determine if your project complies with zoning and applicable laws [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/9273-Building-Permit-Guide-WEB.pdf]
- Draft your own plans or hire a qualified designer to prepare your application and drawings. Note that drawings must be high-quality, properly formatted, flattened, combined in a single PDF, and include all necessary details—sketches are not accepted [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]
- Review the Building Permit Application Guides to ensure you have all required documentation, forms, and fees [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]

**2. Submit Your Application**
- Submit your application and all required documents and forms to **bldapplications@toronto.ca** or online using the Toronto Building Intake Portal [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]
- Ensure your application is complete, including frequently overlooked items like the zoning declaration and tree declaration forms, and that all forms are signed [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]

**3. Initial Sufficiency Review**
- City staff will review your submission within one business day to determine if it is sufficient to make an application [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]
- If insufficient, you will receive a letter containing the additional items required before a review can start [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]
- If sufficient, you will receive a letter requesting payment of initial fees, which can be paid over the telephone via credit card [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]

**4. Plan Review Process**
Once fees are paid and an application is sufficient, staff conduct a thorough review including:
- **Zoning Review**: Verification of compliance with the Zoning By-law regarding land use, building size, location, lot dimensions, parking, and height [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/plan-review-process/]
- **Building Code Review**: Examination for compliance with the Ontario Building Code regarding health, safety, fire protection, structural sufficiency, materials, and plumbing/mechanical systems [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/plan-review-process/]
- **Mechanical Plans Examination** (if applicable): Review of HVAC, plumbing, drainage, and sewage systems [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/plan-review-process/]
- **Fire Prevention Examination** (if applicable): For multi-family residential, commercial, industrial, and institutional applications with fire protection systems [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/plan-review-process/]

**5. Permit Issuance**
- Once your application is reviewed and found to comply with building regulations, and you have paid all required fees, your permit will be issued electronically [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]
- If additional fees are required, you will be notified via email and must make payment before issuance [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]

**6. Construction and Inspections**
- Once you have received your permit, you may begin work on your project [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]
- You must schedule inspections during construction and a final inspection upon completion to close the permit [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/9273-Building-Permit-Guide-WEB.pdf]
- Inspections may be requested online using the Toronto Building Inspection Requests web app [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]

**Important Tips:**
- Apply as early as possible, as back-and-forth may be required to ensure all documents satisfy requirements [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]
- Ensure your project is designed by a qualified professional when required, including projects involving new construction, structural changes, or additions [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]
- You can check the status of your application using the Building Permit Application and Inspection Status tool [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/buildsafeto-learn-about-building-permits/]

prompt: What inspections are required during construction in Toronto?
answer:
Based on the provided evidence, here are the inspection requirements for construction in Toronto:

**Mandatory Inspections at Critical Stages**
The Ontario Building Code requires mandatory inspections at each critical stage of construction. The specific inspections depend on whether your project is classified as a small building (Part 9 of the Ontario Building Code, including houses and small commercial structures) or a large building (Part 3 of the Ontario Building Code) [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/].

**Inspections for Large Buildings (Part 3)**
For large buildings, the following mandatory inspections are required [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/when-to-call-for-inspection-of-large-buildings/]:

*Required Building Inspections:*
- **Footings**: At completion of formwork, before pouring concrete
- **Foundations**: At completion
- **Structural framing**: At completion of structural framing for each storey
- **Fire separations and closures**: At completion of framing for wall, floor and shaft fire separations including closures, continuity and fire stopping, and before applying interior finishes, spray fireproofing and lay-in tiles to ceilings
- **Insulation and vapour/air barrier**: At completion of insulation & vapour/air barrier and before installation of interior services
- **Fireplaces, gas appliances, and chimneys**: At commencement of installation
- **Life safety systems**: At completion of rough-in of the safety systems (referral to Toronto Fire Prevention)
- **Occupancy**: Consult your inspector
- **Final interior inspection**: At completion of interior construction, life safety systems and all fire separations and enclosures
- **Final exterior inspection**: At completion of grading, exterior finishes, fire routes, parking, hydrants and site amenities

*Required Plumbing Inspections:*
- **Site Meeting**: At start of construction (special systems such as pools, window washing etc. should be discussed)
- **Outside storm & sanitary sewers**: At completion, before back filling and ready for testing
- **Water service**: At completion, before back filling and ready for testing
- **Inside storm & sanitary sewers**: At completion (could be partial), ready for testing
- **Rough-in, water supply, drains, waste & vents**: At completion and ready for testing
- **Occupancy**: At completion of installation of all required fixtures
- **Final inspection**: At completion of installation of remaining fixtures
- **Final exterior inspection**: At completion of grading, exterior finishes, fire routes, parking, hydrants and site amenities

**Note**: Construction done in phases may require additional inspections [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/when-to-call-for-inspection-of-large-buildings/].

**Inspections for Small Buildings (Part 9)**
The evidence indicates that separate inspection requirements exist for small buildings (houses and small commercial structures under Part 9 of the Ontario Building Code), but the specific list of mandatory inspections for this category is not provided in the available evidence [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/]. A Building Inspector can assist you in confirming which inspections are required for your particular project [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/].

**General Inspection Requirements**
For all inspections:
- You must request the inspection with a minimum of 48 hours' notice [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/9273-Building-Permit-Guide-WEB.pdf]
- Inspections are conducted Monday to Friday during business hours (8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., excluding statutory holidays) [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/]
- A full scale, coloured print of the permit drawings must be available on site [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/]
- The inspector must be able to see the part of work under inspection; any building elements covered before the related mandatory inspection will have to be uncovered [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/about-building-inspections/]
- A final inspection is required upon completion to close the permit [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/]

**Costs**

prompt: What is an express building permit and do I qualify?
answer:
An **Express Building Permit** is an expedited service for smaller, less complex projects within a predefined scope. The goal is to make the permit-approval process faster and more efficient, with Toronto Building aiming to review eligible applications within **3 business days** after the permit has been taken in [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/express-building-permits/].

**Qualifying Project Types**
You may qualify for Express Services if your project is one of the following:

**Small Residential Projects:**
- Part 9 houses with not more than two dwelling units (and no active building permits for new residential buildings or additions)
- Detached residential ancillary structures (garages, carports, sheds)
- Decks and porches
- Interior alterations
- Basement walkouts and underpinning
- Work impacting a party wall (with enhanced submission requirements)
- Minor fire damage repair
- 1 to 2 unit conversions (no more than 2 dwelling units per building)
- Stand-alone plumbing and drain permits [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/express-building-permits/]

**Small Commercial Projects:**
- Interior alterations to Assembly and Industrial occupancies (Group A & F) up to 300 square metres, with no change in use, no change in patron area, and no active building permits for the building shell
- Interior alterations to Business, Office, Retail, and Restaurants with less than 30 seats (Group D & E) up to 600 square metres, with no change in use, no change in patron area, and no active building permits for the building shell
- Tents (including certified tents)
- Minor fire damage repair
- Stand-alone maglocks [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/express-building-permits/]

**Solar Panels:**
- Solar panel installations attached to an existing building
- All building-mounted stand-alone solar panels [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/express-building-permits/]

**Sign Permits:**
- First Party Signs: up to 3 signs
- Third Party Signs: up to 3 signs [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/express-building-permits/]

**Projects NOT Included in Express Services:**
- Additions to residential dwellings, laneway suites, and garden suites
- Projects requiring Heritage Approval
- Attached garages and carports
- Sign applications for master plans or variances
- Sign permits for more than three signs
- Revisions to permits for projects that included work outside the scope of Express Services [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/before-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/express-building-permits/]

prompt: What happens if I build without a permit in Toronto?
answer:
If you build without a required permit in Toronto, you could face several serious and potentially costly consequences:

**Financial Penalties**
- You will be charged a "work without permit" administrative fee equal to **50 percent of the permit fees** for the project (subject to minimum and maximum values that are updated periodically) [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/working-without-a-permit/]

**Construction Delays**
- All work must **stop immediately** while your permit application is processed, causing delays to your project timeline [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/working-without-a-permit/]

**Remediation Requirements**
- You may be required to **undo work that was already completed**
- You might have to **do additional work** beyond your original plans, such as extra structural or mechanical work to bring the construction up to code [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/working-without-a-permit/]

**Legal and Financial Risks**
- Possible **legal and financial issues** down the road, including impacts on your ability to sell the property or make insurance claims [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/working-without-a-permit/]
- Property owners who fail to comply may face **progressive enforcement measures, including legal action** [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/closing-building-permits/]

**Important Note on Responsibility**
As the homeowner, **you are responsible for paying these fees and penalties yourself**, even if you hired a contractor who assured you that permits were not needed [Source: https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/building-construction/building-permit/after-you-apply-for-a-building-permit/building-inspections/working-without-a-permit/].
judge_reasoning: Answer directly addresses consequences of building without a permit, thoroughly covers all expected concepts (enforcement through legal action, stop work requirement, fine through penalty fees, and orders for remediation), provides specific factual details with multiple relevant Toronto government sources cited for each claim.
